briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Product Drops, Deal Flow, and a Tax Under Pressure: Momentum Builds on Both Coasts of the Industry
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finding real bright spots this week — new product rollouts, a hospitality-driven retail buildout still charging ahead in Muskegon, and both major gubernatorial candidates now promising relief on the 24% wholesale tax. Nationally, the psychedelics sector is sprinting toward FDA approval while Washington just bought the hemp industry another month to fix a looming THC ban.

local.text: Grön, the Wyld-owned edibles brand, just landed its bestselling 'Pearls' gummies on Michigan shelves as part of a four-state rollout, with confirmed placement at Pure Options, High Profile, and Lume — a fresh SKU win for retailers hunting differentiation.

Fields Cannary's ambitious hospitality-driven dispensary-restaurant concept in Muskegon is still moving toward a fall opening, proof that bold retail investment is still happening even as the tax squeezes margins elsewhere in the state.

Jars Cannabis reached a resolution with Madison Heights officials to remove a surveillance camera from its store's parking lot entrance, closing out a years-long dispute tied to the chain's 2022 licensing fight and clearing the path for smoother local operations.

GOP gubernatorial nominee John James is now campaigning on slashing Michigan's cannabis excise tax from 10% to 5% while also promising to rein in unregulated hemp competitors — a signal that tax relief is becoming a genuine bipartisan talking point ahead of November, alongside Democratic rivals who've also pledged repeal of the 24% wholesale levy.

The hard news operators should use as leverage: Michigan's 24% wholesale tax generated only about $37 million in Q2 2026, roughly a third of the $105 million per quarter state officials projected — ammunition for MiCIA's ongoing court appeal and for candidates in both parties now pushing repeal.

national.text: The FDA awarded Commissioner's National Priority Vouchers to Compass Pathways, Usona Institute, and Transcend Therapeutics, compressing standard drug review timelines from roughly ten to twelve months down to just one to two months for their psilocybin and methylone programs — the clearest signal yet that federal approval of psychedelic medicine is accelerating fast.

Compass Pathways is targeting a completed New Drug Application submission for COMP360 psilocybin in Q4 2026, positioning it to become the first classic psychedelic ever approved for a mental health condition.

The FDA has scheduled a public hearing on psychedelic therapeutic use for September 14, 2026, alongside finalized clinical trial guidance covering psilocybin, LSD, and MDMA — real institutional infrastructure being built for what could soon be a live approval docket.

President Trump signed a spending bill delaying the sweeping federal hemp THC recriminalization from November 12 to December 11, buying the hemp and cannabinoid beverage industries another month to negotiate a permanent regulatory framework instead of a blanket ban.

Consolidation is reshaping the MSO landscape: Vireo Growth closed its acquisition of 17 PharmaCann Colorado dispensaries for about $49 million, expanding its footprint to 56 Colorado locations, while Grown Rogue is separately moving to acquire PharmaCann's New York assets — a sign that well-capitalized operators are using distress elsewhere in the market to scale up.
